sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the connection between the oath "be righteous" and Rosh Hashanah, based on the Alter Rebbe's discourse and the concept that every Jew contains a spark of Adam's soul, making Rosh Hashanah the birthday of every Jew.

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing what our sages, of blessed memory, said:
"They administer an oath to him: 'Be righteous, etc.'"
And the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, said
in the name of the Tzemach Tzedek,
that on the first Rosh Hashanah of his life
(the year 5550),
the Alter Rebbe delivered a discourse on "They administer an oath to him: 'Be righteous, etc.'"
And these are the first three chapters of the Tanya.
And one must explain the connection of the concept of "administering an oath to him" to Rosh Hashanah, based on what is explained in Likkutei Torah,
that this that each Jew is called "Adam"
("You are called Adam"),
is
because in the soul of each Jew there is a portion of the soul of Adam the First.
And from this it is understood,
that on Rosh Hashanah
(the day when Adam the First was created),
when there is renewed
(each year)
the matter of the drawing down of the soul of Adam the First into his body
("And He blew
into his nostrils the soul of life"),
this is also the birthday of every Jew.
And it can be said that this is the connection of "administering an oath to him" to Rosh Hashanah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the oath to the month of Tishrei, explaining that the phrase "the seventh month" has three meanings—simple seventh, oath, and satiety—paralleling the three interpretations of the oath.

translations.translation: And this can be connected with the explanation of the Midrash
on the verse:
"In the seventh month, which is the month of oath"
(seventh from the word oath),
and as explained in the discourses of the Tzemach Tzedek,
the connection of "the month of oath" to "They administer an oath to him: 'Be righteous.'"
And perhaps one may add,
that "in the seventh month" has three interpretations:
seventh in its simple sense,
seventh from the word oath
("the month of oath" as above),
and seventh from the word satiety,
as it is brought in the Midrash
that the interpretation of "in the seventh month" is,
that it is satiated with everything
("winepresses within it,
blessings within it,
etc.").
And similarly regarding "They administer an oath to him: 'Be righteous, etc.'",
as explained in many places
and also in the discourses of the Tzemach Tzedek,
that "administer an oath" has three interpretations:
"administer an oath" in its simple sense,
and also from the word satiety and from the word seven,
as will be explained below.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the common theme of oath, satiety, and seven is that an oath binds one's very essence, which is above will, as in the verse "By Myself I have sworn," referring to the level of Atik.

translations.translation: And now, the connection of these three matters
(oath,
satiety,
seven)
is,
that the concept of an oath is that it binds one's very essence.
And as with a simple oath,
that when a person swears to do something
(even though now, at the time he swears, he wants to do it,
so why is the oath needed?),
it is
so that even if something occurs that causes him not to want the thing,
then, by virtue of having sworn to do the thing,
he will do the thing even against his will.
And the reason for this is that the concept of an oath is that it binds one's very essence to this,
the essence of the soul which is above will.
And similarly above,
the concept of an oath is as it is written,
"By Myself I have sworn,"
"By Myself" means by My very essence.
And as explained in the discourses,
that "By Myself" refers to Atik,
and it is known
that Atik is the lowest level within the Emanator, which is above the root of the emanated beings.
